title: Shared vocabulary file
description: One file of rules/vocabulary/. A shared word list is a list SEVERAL rules must agree on, authored once and imported by each of them through detector.shared_vocabulary. THE SPLICED LIST IS NOT STORED ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE: a rule splices a flat list of literals, a reader needs structured metadata per entry, and storing both would be storing the anchors twice — so the flat list is computed from the entries on every read (product/packages/cli/src/vocabulary.ts sharedListItems) and cannot drift from them. A file is not a bundle asset: tools/build-bundle.mjs merges the lists a rule imports into that rule's detector.vocabulary before the bundle is written, so a shipped bundle carries no imports and the scanner never needs this directory.

lists.description: The shared lists this file declares, keyed by the name rules import them under. The name lives here and nowhere else — it is not repeated in the filename and is not aliasable on import, so two rules cannot disagree about what a list is called. Two files declaring one name is a hard error naming both files: which of them a rule got would otherwise depend on directory order.

kind.description: What one entry of this list IS, which decides what an entry must carry. "recipient" is a party that receives data — a payment processor, an analytics vendor, a subprocessor — and every such entry must let a reader see four things without leaving the entry: who it is (vendor), the anchors that spell it in code, what it receives, and the jurisdiction with the source that establishes it. "term" is a concept spelled several ways — an erasure request, a retention period — and carries an identity and a note instead, because a term has no jurisdiction and receives nothing. There is deliberately no default: a list that fell back to "term" would lose the four fields silently, which is the whole reason this field exists.

purpose.description: One sentence: what a rule that imports this list is looking for. It is what an author of the NEXT rule reads to decide whether this list is the right one, and what tells a reviewer whether an entry belongs here or in a different list.

matching.description: How this list's anchors are spelled into every pattern that splices them, in every rule that imports it. IT LIVES ON THE LIST BECAUSE IT IS A FACT ABOUT THE LIST: "a vendor name is typed in whatever case and with whatever separator the ecosystem wants" is true of the anchors, not of any one importing rule, and written in the rules instead it would be re-typed once per importer and drift the first time one of them was edited. Opt-in and inert by absence: a list with no `matching` compiles the byte-identical alternation it compiled before this field existed. Both flags only ever WIDEN what the list matches, so an importing rule may not splice it into match_without, path_without or guard_missing. tools/build-bundle.mjs merges this into each importing rule's detector.vocabulary_matching, exactly as it merges the anchors, so a shipped bundle carries the flags and the scanner never needs this directory.

case_insensitive.description: An anchor's ASCII letters match in either case. Measured 2026-08-27: without it, `recipients-005` reaches `Bamboo.SendGridAdapter` and is silent on `Bamboo.PostmarkAdapter`, `Bamboo.MailgunAdapter` and `Bamboo.MandrillAdapter`, because one vendor was typed with a capital G in this file and three were not. Only ASCII letters fold — a non-ASCII letter has no per-character case mapping.

separator_insensitive.description: A run of `-`, `_` or `.` BETWEEN two alphanumerics matches any of those separators or none, so `help_scout` also reaches `helpscout` and `help-scout`. A leading or trailing run is never flexible, whitespace and `/` are never separators, and a run may never grow. The reverse does not hold and cannot: an anchor with no separator is not made to match a separated spelling, because nothing decides where the split would be. An author who wants both directions spells the SEPARATED form as the anchor.

entries.description: The entries. The spliced alternation is every entry's anchors, in this order, re-sorted longest-first at splice time so no anchor can shadow a longer one that starts with it. One anchor may not appear on two entries of one list: it changes nothing about what matches and it destroys the reader's ability to say which entry a match is evidence of.

vendor.description: Required on a "recipient" list: the party's name as it identifies itself, not as the code spells it. The spellings are anchors; this is who they are spellings OF.

legal_name.description: Optional on a "recipient" list: the receiving party's legal entity by its NAME ALONE, never an address or a note, as the self-name question shows it (product/packages/cli/src/own-name.ts). Written by the list's generator from tools/shared-vocabulary.mjs LEGAL_NAMES, which refuses a name not cut verbatim from this entry's own `vendor` text or holding a standalone number; several entities are joined by " / ". Absent where the research names no single entity.

term.description: Required on a "term" list: the concept the anchors spell, in plain words.

anchors.description: The literal spellings, exactly as they appear in code. LITERAL TEXT, never regular expressions: each is escaped on the way into a pattern, so "(click)" matches the six characters "(click)" and "." matches a full stop. A spelling that needs a boundary guard is written inline in the rule beside the splice, the way a rule's own vocabulary does it.

receives.description: Required on a "recipient" list: what this party receives when the code that carries these anchors runs — the categories of data, in the words a reader of a processing record would use. This is the field that makes the list worth more than a list of names: a rule reports the anchor, and the record needs to say what left the machine.

jurisdiction.description: Required on a "recipient" list: where the receiving party is established, which is what decides whether a transfer question arises at all. A place, not a conclusion — this field never says whether a transfer is lawful.

jurisdiction_source.description: Required on a "recipient" list: where the jurisdiction was read, precisely enough for a reader to check it — the document and the entity it names, with a URL. A jurisdiction with no source is an assertion, and this repository does not ship assertions about parties it has not read.

note.description: Required on a "term" list and optional on a "recipient" one: why this entry is here, or what a reader would otherwise get wrong about it — a spelling that also means something else, a vendor that acquired another, an anchor that is deliberately narrower than it looks.

also_in.description: The OTHER lists this entry also belongs to, by the name each is declared under. ONE RESEARCH RECORD, N MEMBERSHIPS. One research pass stopped at exactly that wall: five researched analytics vendors could not also answer the session-replay question. Four hard errors guard it: a name no file declares, an entry naming its own list, a join between lists of different kind (a kind decides what an entry must carry), and an anchor arriving on top of one the target already has. Chains are not followed — a borrowed copy carries no also_in — so a two-hop membership is written as two names here. Inert by absence: an entry without this field is read exactly as it was before the field existed.

position_bound.description: This entry's anchors may be spliced ONLY inside a clause that anchors them to a construct — a column declaration, a form control, a struct tag, a serialisation key — and never on their own. Only `true` is accepted: `position_bound: false` would be a written-down statement that compiles to nothing, which is the shape detector.vocabulary_matching already refuses one directory away. An entry that is not marked is not thereby declared safe to splice bare — it is only declared small enough that the volume ceiling has nothing to say about it.

near_misses.description: Inline lists a rule spells for ITSELF that are ALMOST this one, recorded here rather than unified into it. A reader deciding whether to unify a divergence is then reading a statement about the rules as they ship.

rules.description: Every rule id whose compiled patterns carry this alternation, and no other. Exact in both directions: a rule that spells the variant and is not named here is a divergence nobody can count.

alternation.description: The branch text as the rule spells it, `|`-separated, with no surrounding parentheses — exactly the characters between the `(` and the `)` of the inline group. It is compared against the rule's COMPILED patterns, so a splice the rule resolves is compared after resolution.

differs_by.description: Why this list stays inline: what it has that the shared list does not, or what the shared list has that it must not acquire. The question a reader has to answer to unify it.

allOf.$comment: kind: recipient — every entry carries vendor, receives, jurisdiction and jurisdiction_source.
kind: term — every entry carries the concept and a note, and none of the recipient fields, which would have no meaning on it.
